handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

title: M3 line-item tuning complete. Woodman blind test at +2.8% with valid logic. Pipeline updated for folder-path holdouts. Ready to test other jobs.
status: M3 TUNED. Four Woodman blind tests run. Nolan satisfied with accuracy. Next: run blind tests on other jobs in the case library.
phase: Phase 1 — Quick Job Budget Generation. M1 = case library (done). M2 = knowledge pack (done). M3 = inference prototype (WORKING, tuned on Woodman). See phase1/PRD_phase1_quick_job_budget_generation.md.
first_thing_next_session: Pick a job from the case library to test next (Killdeer Meadows or Boyds Landing are recommended starting points — simple cul-de-sac jobs that will confirm whether the Woodman fixes generalize). Run: (1) python3 phase1/knowledge_pack/derive_patterns.py --holdout data/<FOLDER>, (2) python3 phase1/inference/m3_infer.py --input 'data/<FOLDER>/<plan>.pdf' --holdout data/<FOLDER> --out phase1/inference/output_<name>/output_<name>.md. Then compare estimate to actuals from the case library.

what_was_done_this_session.full_error_analysis: Ran a complete line-item comparison of test 2 (the blind test from last session) against Woodman actuals. Identified two buckets: ~$65K overestimates and ~$60K underestimates that happened to cancel to +0.3%. Key overestimates: phantom scope items (Signs/Striping, Ped Ramps, Traffic Control, Blow Off — $37K total), drywells (5 vs actual 2 EA, +$10K), Exc to Embank (2× the actual LS). Key underestimates: 12" Ballast price ($11.50 vs $17.40/SY, -$23K), 6" Concrete Approach (missed entirely, -$20K), 1" Water Services price ($2,900 vs $3,300, -$9K).

test_3_improvements.test_3_result: $634,263 vs actual $612,677 = +3.5%. Individual items improved substantially (drywells exact, exc to embank exact, fire hydrants exact, ballast much better) but phantom items (Ped Ramps $14K, Traffic Control $7K, Signs $5K) stayed in because the 3 closest analogs genuinely include them.

test_4_improvement.change: Added arc_loop sewer LF rule: if road_layout == 'arc_loop', use road_LF × 0.80 instead of ROW_SF analog scaling. Data showed cul-de-sac jobs have sewer/road_LF ratio ~0.55-0.59; arc_loop jobs ~0.80.
test_4_improvement.test_4_result: $629,669 vs actual $612,677 = +2.8%. Well inside the 10-15% target with valid derivation logic on every line item.

what_was_done_this_session.pipeline_change_folder_paths: Both derive_patterns.py and m3_infer.py now accept --holdout as a data folder path (e.g. 'data/26001-1_WOODMAN') rather than a job name string. A resolve_holdout() function scans the case library for a matching identity.local_folder and returns (job_name, slug). Error message lists valid folder names if not found.

test_2_blind.verdict: Lucky error cancellation. Not valid accuracy.

test_3_tuned.verdict: Fixes worked on underestimates. Phantom items (Ped Ramps, TC, Signs) remain.

test_4_tuned.verdict: Accepted. Valid logic throughout. Manhole count improved 2→3 (actual 4).

known_remaining_issues_woodman.phantom_items: Ped Ramps (+$14K), Traffic Control (+$7K), Signs No Striping (+$5K) are included because the 3 closest analogs include them. Woodman happens to omit them. This is expected to vary by job — not worth hardcoding an exclusion.
known_remaining_issues_woodman.sewer_connection_count: road_connection_count=2 drives 2 sewer tie-ins, but Woodman actual is 1. Arc roads connect roads at 2 points but sewer may only tie in at 1. No clean fix without Gemini detecting where the sewer stub is.
known_remaining_issues_woodman.6_concrete_approach: Test 4 excluded it (analogs omit it), test 3 included it but overpriced ($12 vs $9.30/SF). This item will vary by job. The KP price for this item needs verification.
known_remaining_issues_woodman.paving_qty: Gemini reads road_LF from stationing (1,000 LF) but actual centerline is 927.65 LF. 8% error propagates to paving SY. No automated fix — Gemini reads station labels, not plan geometry.
known_remaining_issues_woodman.ballast_price: N=2 (Lone Fir $10.50, Mountainside $16.20). Actual Woodman was $17.40 — still above our max. Thin data problem; will improve with more jobs in library.

key_decisions_made_this_session: Nolan confirmed 10-15% overall target is the bar — we are meeting it (+2.8%).
Phantom items (Ped Ramps, Traffic Control) are NOT hardcoded exclusions. They vary by job and the model should learn from analog exclusions_text. Woodman is the outlier.
Water services price → use median, not recency weighting. Recency weighting was pulling to Solara $2,900 when median $3,163 is closer to actual $3,300.
Changing the manhole spacing divisor from 250 makes accuracy worse overall — 250 is the right number. The sewer LF formula is the lever, not the divisor.
Arc-loop sewer LF formula (road_LF × 0.80) is correct based on the data. Cul-de-sac jobs use analog scaling instead.
